The strongest candidate is M4. Its multiplier is m=3 while its mirror partner M3 is m=1 (same W/L), so the first-stage load mirror is 3:1 instead of 1:1. That pulls oa_b high, which turns off the output PMOS M7 and lets M8 pull vout low, consistent with the measured vout of about 0.23 V (offset -0.66 V from 0.9 V). The mismatch also shifts the first-stage bias point, which can change the gm/Cc ratio and push f_unity above the window. The fault description below is an inference from the netlist and measured results, not a confirmed simulation.
